title: Runtime 1.22 — Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack (v1) Release Plan (Draft)
content:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering)
PM: Talia Benson
Exec sponsor: Mateo Alvarez

Doc purpose
- This is the release plan for runtime 1.22 enabling the Hardware Tuning Profiles Pack ("profile pack") in Hosted, plus opt-in availability for Dedicated and guidance for Private.
- This plan focuses on:
  1) Timeline + go/no-go gates
  2) Required sign-offs
  3) Documentation readiness checklist
  4) Backout strategy if perf regressions appear

Scope of the 1.22 release (what we are shipping)
- Runtime can load a versioned profile pack artifact (schema validated) and deterministically select a profile based on detected GPU SKU + driver/CUDA + model/workload bucket.
- Observability tags: profile_id / profile_version / sku. Scheduler queue time metric.
- Feature flag + kill-switch for Hosted canary and staged rollout.
- Guardrailed overrides:
  - Hosted: controlled by fleet defaults; emergency kill-switch supported.
  - Dedicated: opt-in with ability to pin profile_version with audit trail.
  - Private: Helm values / installer warnings and compatibility checks.

Key changes included (non-exhaustive)
- Config loader + schema validation; golden snapshots and CI validation
- Selection logic by SKU + driver version; override precedence rules
- Scheduler workload buckets; queue prioritization for mixed prefill/decode
- H100 attention kernel variant v3 + fallback rules; kernel choice metric
- KV cache compaction thresholds per profile; fragmentation counters
- L40S concurrency cap + headroom tuning
- Provisional B200 SKU detection + compatibility gate (hard fail unless explicitly pinned)
- /health + debug endpoint include active profile metadata (review visibility/security)

Proposed timeline (dates are targets; adjust based on perf canary + doc readiness)

Week of Feb 3, 2026 — Release candidate assembly
- Feb 03 (Tue)
  - Cut runtime-1.22-rc1 branch (Release Eng)
  - Merge window closes for profile-pack-related PRs except critical fixes
- Feb 04–05
  - Benchmark-lab run: baseline matrix on H100 + L40S against rc1 (Rina / Claire / Jonas)
  - Perf-canary config PR lands (Sahana / Rafael) to monitor deltas on canary cohort
- Feb 06 (Fri)
  - Go/no-go #1: “RC quality gate”
    - Criteria:
      - Schema validation + selection tests green
      - No P0 correctness issues in integration tests
      - Benchmark-lab results within acceptance thresholds for H100 + L40S core workloads

Week of Feb 10, 2026 — Hosted canary enablement
- Feb 10 (Tue)
  - Enable feature flag for Hosted canary cohort (1–2% of traffic; controlled regions + model mix)
  - Cohort selection requirements:
    - Include at least one mixed workload route (short prefill/long decode + long prefill/short decode)
    - Include at least one high-concurrency embedding-like workload if applicable
    - Include at least one top customer-like traffic pattern (SRE-approved)
- Feb 10–12
  - Monitor dashboards (Allison / SRE) and daily check-ins with Runtime
- Feb 12 (Thu)
  - Go/no-go #2: “Expand canary”
    - Criteria:
      - SLO guardrails met (see below)
      - No sustained kernel fallback anomalies
      - No OOM/fragmentation alerting trends
      - Perf-canary deltas stable and explainable
  - Expand Hosted canary from 1–2% to 10%

Week of Feb 17, 2026 — Broad Hosted rollout + Dedicated opt-in announcement
- Feb 17 (Tue)
  - If canary looks good: expand Hosted enablement to 50%
  - Start Dedicated opt-in (account-level enablement / pin) with Support/Solutions guidance
- Feb 18–19
  - Final docs review (expected behavior pages + runbooks + troubleshooting)
  - Release notes posted internally; customer messaging draft reviewed (Dedicated)
- Feb 20 (Fri)
  - Go/no-go #3: “Default on in Hosted”
    - If approved: ramp to 100% in Hosted
    - If not: hold at 50% and file follow-ups; do not default-on

SLO + rollout guardrails (blocking conditions)
Owned by SRE (Sean / Rafael) with Runtime support.

Rollout should STOP (hold or rollback) if any of these are true for the canary cohort vs control:
- Latency:
  - p99 end-to-end latency regression > 8% sustained for 30 min on any top-3 routes
  - p95 regression > 5% sustained for 60 min on any top-3 routes
  - Queueing time (scheduler_queue_ms) p95 increases > 20% sustained (indicates batching/backpressure issues)
- Errors:
  - 5xx error rate increases > 0.1% absolute for 30 min (or exceeds existing error budget policy)
  - Elevated timeouts / client disconnects correlated with queueing increase
- Stability / capacity:
  - OOM rate above baseline (even if autorecovered)
  - Fragmentation estimate trending up leading to increasing compaction time
  - Kernel fallback rate above expected for workload bucket and SKU (investigate; may indicate mis-detection or kernel guard too strict)

Notes
- Guardrails are intentionally conservative for this first default-on pack.
- For Dedicated, use stricter gating per-customer during opt-in; avoid mass flips.

Required sign-offs (who must say “yes”)
Release cannot progress past Go/no-go #3 without all sign-offs below.

Engineering / Runtime
- Mateo Alvarez (exec sponsor): overall “ship” decision
- Noah Patel: architecture + selection logic correctness and rollback feasibility
- Hiro Tanaka: H100 kernel variant + fallback correctness, kernel_choice telemetry present
- Sofia Ivanova: scheduler changes risk assessed; queueing metrics validated

Infra & Fleet
- Neha Kapoor (Infra/SRE sponsor): fleet compatibility and operational risk
- Irene Choi: driver/CUDA baseline assumptions validated for Hosted fleet; known variance documented

SRE / On-call readiness
- Sean Gallagher: SLO guardrails + paging plan ready
- Rafael Mendes: rollback automation runbook reviewed; kill-switch semantics tested

Observability
- Allison Grant: dashboards and alert thresholds in place; tags validated for cardinality

Product / Customer impact (Dedicated)
- Lauren Bishop: Dedicated opt-in messaging and “what changes / what can vary” guidance approved

Release engineering
- Connor O’Brien: release checklist complete; changelog discipline; LTS/backport policy set

Documentation readiness checklist (must be COMPLETE before 50%→100% Hosted)
Confluence + internal docs
- Hardware tuning profiles pack overview page up-to-date
- Profile schema + deterministic selection rules page published
- Expected behavior pages complete:
  - H100 expected behavior (latency/throughput buckets, headroom assumptions, failure modes)
  - L40S expected behavior (concurrency caps, stability guidance, OOM/fragmentation prevention)
  - B200 preview page (must emphasize compatibility gate + “not default-on”) 
- Benchmarking matrix and acceptance thresholds page (what we measure + pass/fail)
- Rollout SLO guardrails page (blocking metrics, alerting)
- Observability dashboard spec page (metrics definitions + tags)

Operational runbooks
- “How to validate a new hardware profile” playbook (step-by-step)
- Rollback / kill-switch procedure documented (Hosted + Dedicated + Private sections)
- On-call debug bundle includes active profile metadata (profile_id, profile_version, sku, detected driver/CUDA)

In-repo documentation
- Runtime config reference updated to include:
  - profile_version pin
  - override precedence (fleet default vs customer pin vs emergency kill-switch)
  - compatibility errors and how they manifest

Release notes
- Internal release note: runtime-1.22 profile pack launch
- Dedicated customer messaging draft approved for CSM/Support usage (not necessarily public)

Testing and validation plan (summary)
CI / correctness
- Profile schema validation step required (blocks merges)
- Golden config snapshots updated for 1.22
- Integration tests cover:
  - SKU/driver detection -> profile selection
  - Model reload across GPU pools does not mismatch profile
  - Override guardrails reject unsafe pins

Performance
- Benchmark-lab matrix:
  - Must run for H100 and L40S against rc1 and final
  - Capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory, kernel fallbacks, compaction/fragmentation signals
  - Compare against runtime 1.21 baseline
- Perf-canary:
  - Canary cohort compares deltas on top routes
  - Alerts configured to warn early; some conditions are blocking (see guardrails)

Backout / rollback plan (if perf regression appears)
Principles
- Rollbacks must be fast, observable, and reversible.
- Prefer “disable new default behavior” over “revert runtime binary” unless correctness issue requires code rollback.

Rollback levels (choose minimum necessary)
L0 — Kill-switch: disable profile pack usage (Hosted)
- Action: flip feature flag off for Hosted cohort(s)
- Effect: runtime falls back to pre-1.22 default tuning path (or previous static defaults)
- Time to mitigate: minutes
- Owner: SRE on-call (with Runtime approval); limited to authorized roles
- Audit: record change, cohort, reason, and incident link

L1 — Roll back profile_version default (Hosted)
- Action: set fleet default profile_version back to last known good (e.g., v1.0.0 → v0.9.3)
- Effect: keep profile pack plumbing enabled, but revert to known-stable knob set
- Time: minutes to tens of minutes depending on propagation
- When: when regression is due to specific knob defaults and a previous pack version exists

L2 — Narrow rollback: per-SKU or per-route exclusion
- Action: disable new profiles for affected SKU (e.g., L40S only) or affected workload bucket (mixed long-context)
- Effect: reduces blast radius, maintains improvements elsewhere
- When: regression is SKU-specific or model-family-specific
- Requirements:
  - Selection logic supports compatibility rules / exclusions
  - Clear metrics to confirm mitigation worked

L3 — Binary rollback to runtime 1.21 (last resort)
- Action: rollback runtime deployment
- When:
  - correctness bug, crash loop, or incompatibility that can’t be mitigated via flags/version pin
  - profile pack plumbing itself is causing instability
- Notes:
  - coordinate with Release Eng + SRE; expect longer time due to deployment constraints

Dedicated and Private rollback guidance
Dedicated
- Default posture: opt-in only.
- If customer reports regression:
  - Recommend pinning known-good profile_version (support playbook)
  - If needed, disable new profile selection for customer pool (account-level override)
  - Maintain audit log of pins/rollbacks (required)

Private
- Provide explicit steps:
  - Helm values: set profile_pack.enabled=false or pin profile_version
  - Installer warnings: if incompatible driver/CUDA, advise staying on prior version

Communications plan
Internal
- Go/no-go threads in #eng-releases and #eng-runtime
- Daily canary summary posted during Feb 10–20 window
- If rollback triggered:
  - Post incident-style update with “what changed / current state / next update time”

Customer-facing (Dedicated only; via CSM/Support)
- Share:
  - what the profile pack is (high level)
  - how to pin/rollback profile_version
  - what metrics we monitor and what customer should watch
- Do NOT share:
  - raw internal fleet distributions
  - kernel implementation details beyond supported behavior expectations

Open questions / TODOs (as of last edit)
- Confirm final acceptance thresholds (p99 regression limits) with SRE error budget policy
- Confirm debug endpoint exposure policy (what fields are safe to show to customers)
- Confirm B200 gating behavior in 1.22: hard fail vs warn in Private (currently planned as hard compatibility gate; needs Infra sign-off)
- Confirm LTS/backport policy:
  - Which profile pack fixes qualify for backport without full benchmark matrix rerun?

Changelog discipline
- Every profile pack change must include:
  - profile pack version bump
  - migration notes (what changed, expected impact)
  - links to benchmark-lab runs (artifacts tagged with profile_version + git sha)
  - updated expected behavior doc if behavior changes materially

Appendix: quick reference — operational checks during canary
Dashboards/panels to watch (names TBD; spec owned by Allison)
- Adoption: % traffic by profile_id/profile_version
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 by route/model, split by sku + profile_version
- Queueing: scheduler_queue_ms p50/p95
- Kernel: kernel_choice distribution, kernel_fallback_rate
- Memory: KV cache utilization, compaction time, fragmentation estimate, OOM counters
- Errors: 5xx, timeouts, retries, overload/admission control rejections

If you are on-call and suspect this change is involved
- Check /health or debug bundle for profile_id/profile_version/sku
- Compare against control cohort
- If guardrails breached, initiate L0 rollback (kill-switch) and page Runtime owner on rotation
